title: Scaling Discovery through Test-Time Communication
venue: arXiv:2609.21032v1 (17 Sep 2026); Microsoft Research and UC Berkeley

selection.evidence: Cited by MASS ('at inference time, communicating agents share discoveries'). Chosen deliberately as the strongest PRO-multi-agent result in the chain, to balance an area that had only skeptical findings.

cost.compute_notes: 30-page PDF: Secs 1-3 (ARC-AGI-3, compute ablation, Terminal-Bench null) read; polyomino and MNIST sections skimmed. p01 under 1 s.

triggers: team of communicating agents vs best of k independent

claims.statement: With the same per-agent resources, a team of k communicating agents beats the best of k independent agents on ARC-AGI-3: 8.0% vs 2.2% full-game solve rate at k = 5 (team@5 matches best@33), with fewer total tokens for any solve rate above 1%.
claims.scope: Claude Sonnet 4.6 via Copilot CLI, 25 public games, 64 single-agent trials per game, 20 team trials per game and k, native per-level action budget.

quantities.name: FT09_team3_vs_best3
quantities.source: Sec 3.1; best@3 reproduced from 6/64 (p01 known answer)

our_assessment.why: The per-game effects are far beyond noise. Even if LP85's single-agent rate were at its 95% upper bound (4.6%), best@5 would be about 21% against 65%. The 25-game aggregate is carried by 4 games, which the paper states plainly. The comparison is the right one: equal per-agent compute, best@k from a pool, token curves, and a single agent given 5x the budget. The low-budget ablation shows a coordination tax, and the paper reports it.

claims.statement: Communication helps when progress is verifiable ('verified progress sharing'); on Terminal-Bench 2.0, where feedback does not reliably rank intermediate solutions, team@2 does not beat independent pass@2.

our_assessment.why: The authors report the null in their own paper, which is what makes the positive result credible. It is the same dividing line as SiriuS (verifier: small real gain) against MASS and RHI (LLM judge only: gains hard to separate from noise and completion). And it agrees with wang2026: harness evolution wins on games with granular verifiable feedback and loses on Terminal-Bench.

checked.result: best@3 = 25.9% reproduces from 6/64 by the paper's formula.

Would team@k beat best@k on a task whose only feedback is an LLM judge (MASS's regime)? The paper's own Terminal-Bench null suggests not.
